newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs rebound in Tokyo after two-day fall.
newsitem.headline: JGBs rebound in Tokyo after two-day fall.

text.p: Key March 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rebounded on Thursday after falls over the past two days, backed by the yen's rise against the dollar and losses for the Tokyo stock market.

The key contract jumped in the afternoon on short-covering in light of the dollar's fall toward 121.00 yen and after the Nikkei stock average dropped below the psychologically important 18,000 level. Comments on the economic recovery by the Bank of Japan governor, which were seen as slightly more bearish than before, also provided support, traders said.
The March contract ended up 0.34 at 126.29.
The key contract moved from 126.05 to 126.46 with 43,910 contracts changing hands.

"The JGB market rose in reaction to falls in stocks. But buying did not last long because operators know the market is near its ceiling amid a lack of aggressive buying from investors," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
Traders said investors' firm demand continued especially for newly issued bonds, including corporate bonds, but their buy orders stopped when bond prices became over-par.
"The market cannot find a direction although it (key JGBs) hit a record high on Monday," the dealer said.

After Wednesday's steep fall, the key contract's rebound was helped by a rumour that a foreign hedge fund, which sold about 100 billion yen in the futures market on Wednesday, bought back almost the same amount, traders said.
The key contract plunged to 125.83 on Wednesday, a one-yen fall from the record-high of 126.83 hit on Monday.
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita's comments, which came during the lunch break, were basically the same as before, but traders said the way he talked about private demand was new.
Matsushita said that the central bank's monetary policy was aimed at ensuring a basis for Japan's economic recovery.
Matsushita also said that the recent stock market movements suggested companies were still cautious about Japan's economy.
He added that private-sector demand needed to strengthen to get the economy on a path of self-sustainable recovery. Traders said this meant that the economy was not yet fully on the way to recovery.
There was a vague rumour in the JGB market that a Japanese bank in financial trouble may collapse soon. But many traders said such rumours often appear when banking sector stocks fall.
The yield of key 182nd 10-year cash bonds stood down 0.030 at 2.380 percent at 0739 GMT.
"When looking back, it seems that Monday's record high resulted from an overbought market," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank.
"The market is gradually coming back to a normal range with the key March contract between 125.50 and 126.30," he said.
